evidence.claim: The repository maintains four distinct test dimensions: functional unit/integration, behavioral evals, memory regression, and performance regression.
Integration tests use a binary-under-test approach with mocked LLM responses stored in .responses files.

The integration harness TestRig lives in packages/test-utils/src/test-rig.ts and is re-exported to the integration-tests workspace by integration-tests/test-helper.ts; the helper adds only a skipFlaky flag.
Behavioral evals are split into ALWAYS_PASSES (CI blocking) and USUALLY_PASSES (nightly monitoring).
Memory tests force garbage collection and take V8 heap snapshots to compare against committed baselines with a 10% tolerance.
Performance tests measure wall-clock time, CPU usage, and event loop delay, comparing against baselines with a 15% tolerance.
The integration test suite runs against a sandbox matrix including none, docker, and podman.

No benchmark harness in the repo suppresses or isolates the in-core router or the loop detector for benchmark runs; integration tests inherit production routing behavior and the evals harness mocks responses but not router decisions or loop-check LLM calls.
evidence.notes: Negative finding; absence verified by searching test-utils and evals for router/loop suppression knobs.

contradictions.description: Pollux spec §9 claims 'zero extra API calls / zero latency' for baseline benchmark conditions. Forensic F-07 flags this as over-broad; the tier-1 compartment 07 verified truth VT-07.3 shows the router's ClassifierStrategy emits up to one extra UTILITY_ROUTER LLM call per prompt, and the loop detector emits 0–2 extra LLM calls starting at turn 30. No benchmark knob in this repo suppresses either source today.

risks.description: Stale fixtures in integration tests may mask regressions if the underlying LLM protocol changes.
Flaky USUALLY_PASSES evals might be ignored if not actively monitored in nightly runs.
risks.suggestedGuard: automated alerting on sustained eval degradation

risks.description: Pollux benchmark conditions A/E will report biased numbers unless the harness explicitly pins the router to a single strategy and disables the loop-detection LLM tier; without those controls, baseline runs pay the router/loop-detector overhead that Pollux runs do not (or vice versa).
risks.suggestedGuard: add a BenchmarkHarness in packages/test-utils that accepts an OverrideStrategy-only router and sets LoopDetectionService.llmCheckInterval = Infinity for the run

gaps: Protocol output and agent branching test gaps (OQ-14.1).
No benchmark harness suppresses router/loop-detector side effects (R-14.3, OQ-14.2).

openQuestions: OQ-14.1: Are there specific test gaps for high-risk flows like protocol output and agent branching that lack coverage? Escalate to compartment 12.
OQ-14.2: Which component owns the benchmark harness router/loop suppression knobs — Config, ModelRouterService, or a new test-only shim? Escalate to compartment 07.
